newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends with pared losses in light trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends with pared losses in light trade.

text.p: CME lumber futures rallied from early limit losses of $10.00 per tbf to close slightly lower in light, pre-holiday dealings, traders said.

Futures tumbled for limit losses in January and March early as pressure from the weak cash market pushed prices through technical support and touched off sell stops. Prices recovered as selling lacked followthrough, and short covering and new buying developed in thin dealings, traders said.
The market appeared oversold, even after January fell through the 40-day moving average early, they said.
"It looks like we may have reached a bottom in futures," one trader said.

The seasonal trend is for cash prices to work higher due to declining production during the holidays. Also, cash spruce prices are expected to bottom around $380 per cwt after being up to a record $480 recently when cash markets jumped following the posting of individual mill quotas in Canada, they said.
The National Association of Realtors, NAR, reported that existing home sales declined in October.

NAR said existing U.S. home sales were down to an annual rate of 3.97 million units in October compared with 4.03 million the month before. Their chief economist also predicted a softening economy will cut the annual rate to about 3.85 to 3.9 million units later this year.
